root_cause.text: The rx_complete() function in the CDC Phonet driver lacks bounds checking on the skb_shared_info->frags[] array, allowing a malicious USB device to overflow the array by sending an unbounded sequence of full-page bulk transfers without validating that the fragment count has not exceeded MAX_SKB_FRAGS.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a conditional check `skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS` before calling `skb_add_rx_frag()`. The original code had an unconditional `else` block that would add fragments regardless of how many were already present in the skb, whereas the patched version only adds a fragment if the count is below the maximum limit. When the limit is reached, the skb is dropped and rx_length_errors is incremented instead of continuing to add unbounded fragments.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boundary check to prevent adding fragments beyond MAX_SKB_FRAGS limit and properly handle overflow by freeing the skb and incrementing error statistics.
intent_record.what: Modified the else clause to add a boundary check condition `skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS` before calling `skb_add_rx_frag()`. Added a new else block that frees the skb, nullifies the rx_skb pointer, and increments the rx_length_errors statistic when the fragment limit is exceeded.
intent_record.how: Previously, the code would unconditionally attempt to add a fragment to the skb regardless of how many fragments were already present. Now it checks if the skb has room for another fragment before adding it. If the fragment limit (MAX_SKB_FRAGS) is reached, the skb is freed, the rx_skb state is cleared, and an error counter is incremented instead of attempting an invalid fragment addition that could cause buffer overflow or memory corruption.

bic_trace_step.reason: The rx_complete() function (lines 156-207) contains the vulnerable construct. Specifically, at lines 169-172 and 174-176, the function calls skb_add_rx_frag() to add fragments to the skb without any bounds checking on skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags. The code unconditionally adds fragments: 'skb_add_rx_frag(skb, skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags, page, 1, req->actual_length)' and later 'skb_add_rx_frag(skb, skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags, page, 0, req->actual_length)'. A malicious USB device can send an unbounded sequence of full-page bulk transfers (PAGE_SIZE bytes), and since req->actual_length < PAGE_SIZE only triggers the end condition (line 177), a device sending exactly PAGE_SIZE repeatedly will keep adding fragments indefinitely without checking against MAX_SKB_FRAGS. There is no validation that nr_frags has not exceeded the maximum allowed fragments before calling skb_add_rx_frag().
